note.keys: Ed25519 private keys are SHA-256 of 'ori runtime-posture/v1 <label> test key', labels 'posture A' and 'posture B'. Test keys only.
note.records: Each record case is one message on the topic of `topic_device`, judged at checks 3 to 10 of Receiving by a gateway configured with `configured_devices` and `pinned_keys` whose wall clock reads `gateway_wall_ms`; `expected` is `pass` or the reason. Checks 1 and 2 are gateway-api/v2's corpora's.
note.sequences: Each sequence runs its events in order against one gateway. `receive` judges a message and gives its verdict, its store write failing when `store_write` is `fails`, or outstanding past 1000 ms when it is `stalls`, whose `states` are those once that bound has passed; `observe` reads the state; `restart` restarts the gateway, resetting its monotonic clock and its last refusals, starting from the store as it was last written, finding it unreadable when `store_readable` is false, and installs `pinned_keys` and `configured_devices` when given; `store_read_succeeds` is a read of an unreadable store that succeeds, finding the store as it was last written, which is empty when the sequence starts unreadable; and `store_write_completes` a write of the state in memory that completes, either the outstanding one or a retry. The two causes never hold together. `store_readable` false starts with the store unreadable, for the reason `store_condition` names. A write that would change nothing durable is not made, so `store_write` has no effect on it. `wall_ms` and `mono_ms` are the gateway's wall and monotonic clocks at the event. `expected` holds the verdict, for a receive, and in `states` the state of each device configured after the event, each a judgement the gateway makes then, so a record that reads `stale` stays `stale` until a fresh one is accepted, with `reason`, `record_b64`, `received_at_ms`, `last_refusal` and `last_refusal_at_ms` as Carriage gives them: each is the device's `posture_record` in Site Health, and its object in the LAN posture body without `device_id`.
note.config: gateway-config/v2 posture key load rules, after gateway.state_directory's, whose value here is null or one absolute path of printable ASCII with no space; gateway-config/v2's state-directory corpus judges every other value. With gateway.auth and evidence disabled: `valid`, and `rule` when refused. `runtime_keys` lists its entries in the order they are written.
note.readback: Owned by the runtime, which serves it; a gateway does not consume these cases. `request` is the frame's body, the bytes before its first LF, and holds no LF; the socket's framing is operator-socket/v3's and is not judged here. operator-socket/v3 runtime_device_key: the request bytes, the peer (`root`, `operator`, `other` or null when credentials cannot be established), whether the posture key is loaded, the device and key it would answer, and the answer, whose `detail` is never compared.

sequences.name: accept_then_age
sequences.note: A record is current until its age passes 900000 ms, then stale.

sequences.name: higher_refreshes
sequences.note: Each strictly higher record restarts the age.

sequences.name: replay_refreshes_nothing
sequences.note: The held record received again is replayed and does not refresh its age.

sequences.name: receipt_age_counts
sequences.note: A record received 300000 ms after it was signed is current for 600000 ms more.

sequences.name: future_receipt_age_floored
sequences.note: A record signed ahead of the gateway's clock has receipt age 0.

sequences.name: wall_step_back_never_freshens
sequences.note: A wall clock stepped back leaves the monotonic elapsed time in force.

sequences.name: wall_step_forward_stales_early
sequences.note: Elapsed time is the greater of the monotonic and wall elapsed times, so a suspend the monotonic clock did not count, or a forward wall step, stales the record.

sequences.name: wall_forward_then_back_stays_stale
sequences.note: A wall clock stepped forward stales the record; stepped back again, it lowers the wall elapsed time, but a record that has read stale stays stale.

sequences.name: stale_at_boundary_then_back
sequences.note: One millisecond past the bound on the wall clock is stale, and a step back to the bound itself does not make it current again.

sequences.name: replay_does_not_end_stale
sequences.note: A replayed copy of a record that has read stale leaves it stale; a fresh record ends it.

sequences.name: lower_tuple_sticky
sequences.note: A validly signed lower record makes the device unknown until a higher one.

sequences.name: lower_boot_sticky
sequences.note: A record of an earlier boot is lower, whatever its sequence.

sequences.name: stale_timestamp_sets_nothing
sequences.note: An old record refused at check 10 sets no sticky reason.

sequences.name: equal_pair_conflict
sequences.note: An equal pair with different bytes is a conflict, sticky until a higher record.

sequences.name: issued_regression_conflict
sequences.note: A higher pair whose issued_at_ms is more than 300000 ms below the held record's is a conflict.

sequences.name: issued_regression_edge_accepted
sequences.note: 300000 ms below the held record's is accepted.

sequences.name: restart_reads_stale
sequences.note: After a gateway restart the held record is stale until a fresh one arrives; the retained redelivery is replayed.

sequences.name: sticky_survives_restart
sequences.note: A sticky reason survives a gateway restart.

sequences.name: repin_keeps_each_key
sequences.note: A pin changed to B and back to A resumes A's held state, so an old A record stays lower.

sequences.name: repin_new_key_no_record
sequences.note: A new pin with nothing held under it reads unknown(no_record), and the old key's records are key_mismatch.

sequences.name: negated_pin_shares_state
sequences.note: A pin changed to A's negation reads A's held state: the two are one recognised key, so a lower record signed under the negation is lower.

sequences.name: refusal_keeps_sticky
sequences.note: A record refused at checks 1 to 10 clears no sticky reason.

sequences.name: later_sticky_replaces
sequences.note: A later sticky reason replaces an earlier one.

sequences.name: equal_conflict_keeps_held
sequences.note: A conflict leaves the held record as it was: the original replayed is replayed, and the conflict stays.

sequences.name: greater_conflict_keeps_held
sequences.note: An issued-regression conflict leaves the held record as it was, so a later genuine record at the same pair is accepted.

sequences.name: regression_judged_on_issued
sequences.note: The regression bound compares issued_at_ms values, not the wall clock at the held record's receipt.

sequences.name: conflict_then_lower
sequences.note: A lower record after a conflict replaces the sticky reason.

sequences.name: sticky_past_age
sequences.note: A sticky reason stays unknown past the age bound, never stale.

sequences.name: repin_returns_sticky
sequences.note: A sticky reason belongs to its key: re-pinned to B, B reads clean; back to A, A's reason returns.

sequences.name: higher_boot_lower_seq
sequences.note: A higher boot generation orders above every record of a lower one.

sequences.name: stale_retained_after_restart
sequences.note: After a gateway restart, a retained record older than the skew bound is stale_timestamp, and the device stays stale.

sequences.name: last_refusal_shows_key_mismatch
sequences.note: A device whose records all arrive under another key shows the reason.

sequences.name: two_devices_independent
sequences.note: Two devices hold independent states and sticky reasons.

sequences.name: store_unavailable_one_unpinned
sequences.note: With the store unavailable, a pinned device is store_unavailable and an unpinned one no_pinned_key.

sequences.name: store_corrupt
sequences.note: A corrupt store reads as an unreadable one.

sequences.name: store_write_fails_closed
sequences.note: A failed write keeps its verdict and change in memory and makes the store unavailable; it stays so as time passes, a completed write of the state in memory clears it, and the conflict then shows.

sequences.name: store_write_stalls_closed
sequences.note: A write still outstanding 1000 ms after it began fails closed; when it completes late, the state it wrote is in force.

sequences.name: store_unreadable_then_read
sequences.note: An unreadable store clears when a read succeeds; the read finds an empty store, so no record is held.

sequences.name: noop_write_cannot_fail
sequences.note: A sticky reason set again to the one held writes nothing, so a failing store cannot fail it.

sequences.name: store_write_fails_all_devices
sequences.note: A failed write blanks every pinned device, not only the one it was for.

sequences.name: restart_loses_unwritten_change
sequences.note: A change held only in memory, its write failed, is lost at a restart: the gateway starts from the store as last written, so the lower_tuple it had shown is gone and the earlier run's record reads stale.

sequences.name: store_write_stalls_other_device_waits
sequences.note: A write stalled past its bound blanks every device; a record for another device arriving once the bound has passed, with the write still outstanding, is store_unavailable and changes nothing, and the late write, carrying the whole state in memory, restores both devices.

sequences.name: restart_unreadable_then_read
sequences.note: A store unreadable at a restart hides every device; the read that then succeeds finds the store as last written, and its record, received in the earlier run, reads stale.

sequences.name: last_refusal_is_latest
sequences.note: The last refusal is the most recent one, with the wall clock at its receipt, and a later accepted record does not clear it.

sequences.name: restart_clears_last_refusal
sequences.note: A last refusal is since the gateway started, so a restart clears it.

sequences.name: removed_device_keeps_state
sequences.note: A device removed from the configuration keeps its state, which serving it again resumes.

sequences.name: no_pin
sequences.note: No pinned key: unknown(no_pinned_key), and records are refused.

sequences.name: store_unavailable
sequences.note: An unreadable store: unknown(store_unavailable), nothing accepted.

sequences.name: store_unavailable_no_pin
sequences.note: No pin while the store is unreadable reads no_pinned_key.

sequences.name: store_unavailable_refusal_first
sequences.note: With the store unreadable, a record refused at checks 1 to 10 is refused for its reason.

config.name: duplicate_negated_key

config.name: no_state_directory

config.name: order_state_directory_first

config.name: order_device_before_key

config.name: order_entry_by_entry

config.name: order_code_point

config.name: order_rule_3_entry_by_entry

config.name: whitespace_value

config.name: whitespace_key
config.note: A key with surrounding whitespace names no configured device.

config.name: unknown_and_malformed_entry
config.note: One entry that is both an unknown device and a malformed value.

config.name: order_entry_before_duplicate
config.note: A malformed entry is named before a duplicate of two other entries.

readback.name: readback
readback.note: The installed operator reads the key.

readback.name: extra_member
readback.note: A member the operation does not accept.

readback.name: key_not_loaded
readback.note: The posture key is not loaded in this run.

readback.name: form_before_caller
readback.note: An unaccepted member from an unadmitted peer: form first.

readback.name: caller_before_key
readback.note: An unadmitted peer while the key is not loaded: the caller first.

readback.name: operation_case_variant
readback.note: A member that differs from operation only in case.

readback.name: operation_escaped
readback.note: operation written with an escape is operation.

readback.name: over_bound_before_form
readback.note: Over the bound and not JSON: the bound is decided first.
